explanations.answer: The district of Tyre and Sidon
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. Matthew says Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21). That's where our story happens. A woman from that region is about to come to Him.

Close, but that's not the spot in this passage. The text says, “Leaving that place, Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon.” So the whole story takes place in the district of Tyre and Sidon. I'd have packed for Galilee too, so no shame here.
Nope, the text sends Him somewhere else. Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon. That's where this woman meets Him. Judea is a fine guess, but it's not on this map.

explanations.answer: Her daughter is possessed by a demon
explanations.explanation: Right on the money. She cries out, “My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.” That's the reason she's calling for mercy. She's asking for herself, but the whole cry is about her girl.

explanations.answer: Her husband is sick with a fever
explanations.explanation: Not this time. The woman tells Jesus, “My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.” The text talks about her daughter and gives us nothing about a husband. Keep your eyes on the daughter, friend, because the whole story is about her.

explanations.answer: Her son has been blind from birth
explanations.explanation: That's a different story, friend. In this passage, the woman says, “My daughter is miserably possessed by a demon.” So the one in trouble is her daughter, and the text doesn't mention a son. Easy to mix up, since the Gospels have a lot of people asking for help.

This one is the opposite of what the text says. It says, “But Jesus did not answer a word.” She asks for mercy and gets silence back. You know that feeling when someone leaves you on read? Same kind of quiet.
That's right, it's false. The text says, “But Jesus did not answer a word.” She cries out and no answer comes. I think that's a heavy moment for her.

You got it, baker. His disciples came and urged Him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.” They didn't just mention it, they urged Him. That's a strong word, and it tells us how much they wanted her sent off.

It's actually true, so let's look at the text. His disciples came and urged Him, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.” They're asking Jesus to send her off. Good news is, the story keeps going.
Yes, crying out. The disciples say, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.” Keeps is the key word, because she isn't stopping. I think I'd lose my voice by lunch.
Whispering would've been a lot quieter, friend. The disciples say she “…keeps crying out after us.” That's a loud one, not a soft one. Nobody has to lean in to hear her.
Staring is a fair guess, but that's not what the text says. The disciples tell Jesus, “Send her away, for she keeps crying out after us.” The reason they give is her crying out. Not her eyes.

explanations.answer: The lost sheep of the house of Israel
explanations.explanation: That's it. Jesus answers, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” After the silence, those are the words He says. It's a hard thing to read, and I think it's a heavy moment.

explanations.answer: The scribes and elders of Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Not quite. Jesus says, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” He doesn't name scribes or elders in His answer to her. It's all about the lost sheep.

explanations.answer: The faithful ones in every nation
explanations.explanation: That's not what He says here. His words are, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” He names the house of Israel, not every nation. Tough to read, but that's what the text gives us.
The text goes the other way. After Jesus says that, “The woman came and knelt before Him.” She doesn't leave, she comes closer. I'd have been halfway to the parking lot.
That's right, she doesn't leave. The text says, “The woman came and knelt before Him.” Then she says, “Lord, help me!” Silence and a hard answer, and she still comes closer.

That's right, she accepts it. She says, “Yes, Lord,” and then uses the same picture: “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.” She doesn't argue with it. She picks it up and answers from inside it.
Look at how she starts. She says, “Yes, Lord,” which is not a push back. Then she adds, “even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.” She stays inside the picture Jesus gave.

She's not skipping over it, friend. Her answer begins with “Yes, Lord,” and then talks about dogs eating crumbs that fall from their master's table. That's the very picture Jesus gave, with the children's bread and the dogs. She builds right on it.
That's the word. Jesus says, “O woman, your faith is great!” Out of everything in this scene, that's what He points to. Faith is the word He picks.
Her answer was sharp, I'll give you that. But Jesus says, “O woman, your faith is great!” The word He picks is faith. That's what He praises.

She cries out and she kneels before Him, so I see why you picked courage. But the word Jesus uses is faith: “O woman, your faith is great!” He doesn't say courage here. I think I'd have lost my nerve at the silence.
Yes, He does. Jesus says, “Let it be done for you as you desire.” Think about how this started, with a woman crying out for help and getting no answer. Now she hears those words.

It's actually true, so here's what the text says. Jesus answers, “Let it be done for you as you desire.” That's after she tells Him about the crumbs. So what she's asking for is exactly what He grants.
Yes, that very hour. The text says, “And her daughter was healed from that very hour.” No waiting around for a timer to ding. The healing is tied to that very hour.
That's later than the text says. It says, “And her daughter was healed from that very hour.” So the healing doesn't wait for morning. It's the same hour He speaks.
A whole week would be a long wait, friend. The text says her daughter “…was healed from that very hour.” So there's no week of waiting in this story. The healing comes in that very hour.
